newsitem.title: CHINA: Cathay posts 35 pct drop in interim net.
newsitem.headline: Cathay posts 35 pct drop in interim net.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd posted a 35 percent drop in interim net profit on Wednesday, with the grounding of its Airbus fleet, a slump in Japanese traffic and weak currencies dealing a blow to its performance.
The Hong Kong carrier said net profit dropped to HK$1.07 billion from HK$1.65 billion in the same 1996 period. The 1996 figure included an exceptional gain of HK$541.0 million.
Turnover during the first six months of the year rose to HK$15.78 billion compared with HK$15.16 billion.
"The first half of 1997 presented a series of difficult challenges for Cathay Pacific," chairman Peter Sutch said.
"Currency fluctuations, a weak summer travel market and the brief suspension of A330-300 operations created a number of obstacles for the airline," he said in a statement.
Cathay Pacific suspended service of its 11 A330-300s in late May after three inflight engine shutdowns on Cathay and a fourth on Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd. Service resumed by June 10.
Sutch said at the time he expected the grounding to slice between HK$120 million and HK$150 million from the airline's bottom line this year.
"Other events which had an impact on revenues in the first half of the year included a much anticipated summer travel peak that failed to materialise," Sutch said on Wednesday.
Hong Kong saw a significant fall in visitors from Japan, an important source of revenue for Cathay Pacific.
The Japanese yen also suffered from U.S. dollar strength.

Cathay Pacific said passenger load factors had declined substantially since May. "Overall revenue load factor was up slightly during the first half, averaging 71.2 percent, but downward pressure on yields and the weakness of certain European currencies reduced revenues on many routes," it said.

Cathay's net operating profit fell to HK$1.13 billion during the first half of the year from HK$1.17 billion in the 1996 period. It had no exceptional items compared with last year's gain on the sale of a 12.21 percent stake in Dragonair.
Cathay Pacific Cargo posted a rise of 13.6 percent in turnover to HK$2.98 billion, equivalent to 20.5 percent of Cathay Pacific Airway's total traffic turnover.
"We have exceeded our targets and taken advantage of some excellent opportunities to boost yields and revenue," Cathay Pacific's General Manager Cargo James Barrington said.
Cathay said it expected to see an improvement in its results for the second half of the year but analysts said full-year earnings estimates may need to be downgraded.

"As in previous years we expect the results for the second half year to show an improvement over those for the first half, although operating conditions are clearly going to stay difficult with yields continuing to be under pressure and some markets remaining soft," Cathay Pacific said.
Steven Thompson, chief analyst at Nikko Securities, said he had been expecting net profit for the full year of HK$4.0 billion compared with HK$3.81 billion reported in 1996.
"That might be a little bit difficult to achieve now. On the whole it looks like I will have to downgrade," he said.

SocGen-Crosby Securities head of research Robert Sassoon said while the second-half was normally weighted in Cathay Pacific's favour, with more travel particularly around the Christmas period, the Japanese market was weak.
"1997 may not turn out to be a particularly good year," he said. "Load factors have been down over the last couple of months and that is a worrying trend and currency is also key."
Analysts said there could be some weakness in Cathay shares on Thursday although investors had anticipated disappointing results. The stock fell HK$0.20 on Wednesday to HK$14.00.
